chunks: 4576 - Jamil narrated from Fudayl, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: "May I be your ransom! Some of our companions have narrated from you that you said: if a man makes lawful for his believing brother the private part of his bondwoman, then she is lawful for him." So he said to him: "Yes, O Fudayl."

I said: "What do you say regarding a man who has a precious bondwoman, and she is a virgin; he makes lawful for a brother of his what is short of the private part. Does he have the right to deflower her?" He said: "No. He has only what was made lawful for him from her. Even if he made lawful for him a kiss from her, what is beyond that would not be lawful for him."

I said: "What if he made lawful for him what is short of the private part, but desire overpowered him and he deflowered her?" He said: "That is not proper for him." I said: "If he did that, would he be a fornicator?" He said: "No, but he would be treacherous, and he must pay her owner one-tenth of her value."

key_terms.أَحَلَّ: made lawful or permitted in a specific legal sense
key_terms.خَائِنًا: treacherous; one who violates a trust
key_terms.عُشْرَ قِيمَتِهَا: one-tenth of her value as compensation
key_terms.فَرْجَ: the private part, referring here to intercourse

ai.seo_question: If someone is permitted intimacy short of intercourse with a bondwoman, can he go beyond what was specifically allowed?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a legal ruling regarding the limited permission granted over a bondwoman and makes clear that only the specifically authorized act is lawful. If a person exceeds that permission, he is not described here as a fornicator, but as one who has betrayed trust and is financially liable to the owner.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4576 - Jamil narrated from Fudayl, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (as): "May I be your ransom! Some of our companions have narrated from you that you said if a man permits his believing brother to have relations with his bondwoman, then she is lawful for him."
Imam (as) said: "Yes, O Fudayl."

I asked: "What do you say about a man who has a precious bondwoman who is a virgin, and he permits his brother to enjoy her, but only in ways other than intercourse? Is it permissible for him to deflower her?"
Imam (as) said: "No, he is only allowed what has been made lawful for him. Even if he permitted him only to kiss her, nothing beyond that would be lawful for him."

I asked: "What if he permitted him everything except intercourse, but his desire overcame him, and he deflowered her?"
Imam (as) said: "He should not do that."
I asked: "If he did, would he be considered a fornicator?"
Imam (as) said: "No, but he would be a betrayer and must compensate the owner of the bondwoman with one-tenth of her value."
